title: Lay a click-lock vinyl floor tile: angle its tongue into the laid row's groove, then lower it flat to lock
instruction: Click the loose vinyl tile into the laid row: angle its tongue into the groove, end against the spacer, lower it flat, then let go.
context: Rigid-core vinyl and laminate floors float: no glue or nails, each tile held only by its click joints. Each new tile's long tongue edge is angled about 20 deg into the groove of the row already laid, pushed home along its whole length and lowered flat, dropping its locking tooth behind the row's locking bump. Lowered too soon, it rides on the bump: a raised edge and an open seam the next row cannot lock to. Done for every tile by carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00: 'Install structures or fixtures, such as windows, frames, floorings, trim, or hardware...'; 889,700 US jobs) and floor layers (47-2042.00). Hard: the 600 mm, 1.55 kg tile is held only at its near edge while its out-of-reach tongue must enter a 1.4 mm mouth evenly along its length. Unlike #722, #123 or BEHAVIOR's laying wood floors (boards set side by side, no joint) or #37 (a DIN module hooked onto a rail), a 600 mm joint is angled shut and locked.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left, z up from the table top; arm bases at (0, +/-0.305). The table top is the subfloor. Tiles: MSI Trecento rigid-core luxury vinyl tile (White Ocean, VTRWHIOCE12X24-5MM-12MIL), 0.600 x 0.300 x 0.005 (4 mm stone-polymer core over a 1 mm attached IXPE pad), 1.55 kg (35 lb case of 10, less the carton). Long-edge angle-in click profile (mm, from the pad's underside; README has the full section): groove edge = upper lip 1.4 thick over a groove 1.4 tall and 3.0 deep, and a strip 2.2 thick running 7.0 past the top joint line with a locking bump 1.6 wide, 1.5 tall at its end (locking face leaning back 62.5 deg, top corners chamfered 0.3); tongue edge = tongue 1.0 thick, 2.6 long, bevelled underneath, and a locking tooth that sits between bump and joint with 0.2 play. The tongue gets under the lip only with the tile tipped 12 deg or more. Laid row, fixed: a 0.300 cut piece (y -0.300..0) and a full tile (y 0..0.600), x 0.460..0.760, groove edge toward the robot with its top joint line at x 0.460, its strip reaching x 0.453. Wall: 18 mm plywood, 0.100 tall, fixed, face at y -0.3095, x 0.180..0.780. Spacers: two blue plastic 3/8 in (9.5 mm) flooring spacers, 0.040 long (x), 0.030 tall, fixed against the wall face: the new row's at x 0.390..0.430, the laid row's at x 0.590..0.630, so tiles end at y -0.300. Batten: sawn pine, 47 x 50 mm, 0.200 long, fixed, x 0.1045..0.1515, y -0.100..0.100, 0.050 tall. Loose tile, free: tongue edge away from the robot, set against the row and not engaged: its tongue rests on the laid row's locking bump with its far top edge at x 0.452 (8 mm short of the seam), 1.1 mm above the laid tiles' top; its near edge lies on the batten's far top edge, so it is tipped up 9.2 deg (near top edge at x 0.156, 0.055 up); its ends at y -0.290 and +0.310 (10 mm from the new row's spacer). Goal: x 0.160..0.460, y -0.300..0.300, flat, locked, end on the spacer. Friction (static/dynamic): tile and laid row 0.4/0.3 (vinyl), batten, wall and spacers 0.5/0.4.
scoring: Measured on the loose tile only, after the robot lets go. Seam: the gap between the tile's far top edge and the laid row's top edge (x 0.460), measured 10 mm in from each end (feeler gauge). Lippage: the tile's top beside the seam against the laid tiles' top, at each end (straightedge and feeler gauge). Near edge: the tile's near top edge height above lying flat, at each end. End gap: the wall face to the tile's end at the new row's spacer (ruler). An end is LOCKED when its seam is 0.4 mm or less (and not overlapping the row by more than 2 mm), its lippage within 0.5 mm, and its near edge within 1 mm of flat; in a real trial confirm it with a 10 N pull on the near edge, flat along the floor toward the robot, which must not open the seam past 0.4 mm. An end is AGAINST THE ROW when its seam is 10 mm or less (overlap at most 2 mm) and its near edge is within 2 mm of flat. Every credit needs the tile released (each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from the tile's bounding box) and at rest (its near corners and far edge moving under 0.5 mm per 50 ms step), held for 1 s. 1.0: both ends locked and end gap 12 mm or less (the spacer gives 9.5). 0.75: both ends locked, end gap over 12 and up to 40 mm. 0.5: both ends locked with end gap over 40 mm, or one end locked and both against the row (racked: the other end riding on the bump). 0: anything else, including a tile lowered before its tongue was in (riding on the bump along its length: seam open, about 1.4 mm high), the untouched start (still tipped on the batten), a tile still held or still moving, tipped up, lying on top of the laid row, short of the row, or off the table. Sticky 0: the tile ever drops off the table. Success = 1.0 held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at step 447 (22 s)
reset_notes: To unlock, lift the tile's near edge to about 25 deg and draw it back out of the groove. Set it back against the row: tongue resting on the laid row's locking bump with its far top edge 8 mm short of the seam, near edge on the batten, ends at y -0.290 and +0.310. Nothing is consumed; replace a tile whose tongue, bump or lip is chipped.
fidelity: The tile is rigid (real SPC flexes slightly), with one friction value for its vinyl and its foam pad. The click profile is an angle-in (Valinge 2G-type) section scaled to the 4 mm core, as convex collision pieces with 0.1-0.2 mm clearances: it locks by contact alone, nothing scripted, without the small snap of a real strip flexing. Short-edge profiles are not modelled (no end joint is made). The tile starts on the lip and a batten, as a person would set it: the robot cannot lift its far edge.
